National Coverage Determination (NCD) 20.8.3
Single Chamber and Dual Chamber Permanent Cardiac Pacemakers
Medicare National Coverage Determinations Manual, Publication 100-03, Chapter 1, Part 1, Section
20.8.3. Effective date: 08/13/2013. Implementation: Transmittal 170 (CR 8525).
Applies to Medicare Advantage plans, including UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage, which follow CMS National Coverage
Determinations for cardiac pacemakers. Reproduced for software testing from the published NCD and the UF Health
Jacksonville compliance checklist of NCD 20.8.3 (10/22/2018); wording reconstructed, verify against cms.gov before clinical
use.
A. General
A permanent cardiac pacemaker is an implanted device that provides electrical stimulation to the heart to
maintain an adequate heart rate. This section addresses single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent
cardiac pacemakers. It does not address biventricular pacemakers, devices that stimulate more than two
chambers, devices intended to treat tachyarrhythmias or cardiac dyssynchrony, cardiac resynchronization
therapy, or self-contained pacemaker monitors.
B. Nationally Covered Indications
Effective for claims with dates of service on and after August 13, 2013, CMS covers single-chamber or
dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers when ALL of the following are met:
1. The patient has documented bradycardia; AND
2. The bradycardia is non-reversible (not due to a transient or correctable cause); AND
3. The bradycardia is symptomatic, with documented symptoms directly attributable to the bradycardia (for
example syncope, near-syncope, dizziness, confusion, exercise intolerance, heart failure symptoms); AND
4. The bradycardia is due to ONE of the following:
• Sinus node dysfunction (sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, sinus arrest, sinoatrial block,
chronotropic incompetence); OR
• Second-degree and/or third-degree atrioventricular (AV) block.
C. Nationally Non-Covered Indications
Single-chamber and dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers are not covered for the following:
• Bradycardia due to reversible causes, such as electrolyte abnormalities, medications or drugs, and
hypothermia.
• Asymptomatic first-degree AV block.
• Asymptomatic sinus bradycardia.
• Asymptomatic sinoatrial block or sinus arrest.
• Ineffective atrial contractions (such as chronic atrial fibrillation or flutter, or giant left atrium) without
symptomatic bradycardia.
• Asymptomatic second-degree AV block of Mobitz Type I, unless the QRS complexes are prolonged
or electrophysiological studies demonstrate that the block is at or beyond the level of the His bundle.
• Syncope of undetermined cause.
• Bradycardia during sleep.
• Right bundle branch block with left axis deviation (and other forms of fascicular or bundle branch
blocks) without syncope or other symptoms of intermittent AV block.
• Asymptomatic bradycardia in post-myocardial infarction patients about to initiate long-term
beta-blocker drug therapy.
• Frequent or persistent supraventricular tachycardias, except where the pacemaker is specifically for
the control of the tachycardia.
• A clinical condition in which pacing takes place only intermittently and briefly, and which is not
associated with a reasonable likelihood that pacing needs will become prolonged.
D. Other
All other indications for single-chamber or dual-chamber permanent cardiac pacemakers not otherwise
indicated as covered or non-covered above remain at local Medicare Administrative Contractor discretion.

Diagnosis codes and modifier requirements are specified in Local Coverage Article A54926.
Documentation should include the rhythm diagnosis, the symptoms attributed to the bradycardia and their
correlation with the rhythm, and the exclusion of reversible causes (including review of rate-slowing
medications and metabolic workup).
